entries.reason: a caller's own visitor adopts the protocol, so the library has to carry the protocol object for the adoption to be found at run time
entries.effect: the protocol and its eleven visit methods are carried; -[CNChangeHistoryEvent acceptEventVisitor:] and the three concrete classes ask whether the visitor adopts it before handing the event over, so a visitor that does not is sent nothing
entries.source: the header of Contacts/CNChangeHistoryEvent.h in the SDK 16.4, which declares the protocol and its eleven methods; Contacts/CNChangeHistoryEvent13.m of this package, whose three acceptEventVisitor: bodies now ask conformsToProtocol: first - which is also what makes this library carry the protocol object, measured as the __OBJC_PROTOCOL_$_CNChangeHistoryEventVisitor its object defines

entries.reason: the me card is iOS 10.11: iOS 6.1.3 has no Contacts framework and no record of the person who owns the device in the address book it does have, so there is no card to hand back
entries.effect: nil, and the error out-parameter is an NSError in CNErrorDomain with code CNErrorCodeRecordDoesNotExist (200) and the description saying this release has no me card; a nil error pointer is allowed and nothing is written, and the keys are not read, since there is no contact to read them out of
entries.source: the host's own Contacts under MacOSX.sdk, asked for a me card it has no access to: nil with CNErrorCodeAuthorizationDenied (100) and two userInfo keys, which is a refusal of access rather than the absence of a card and is a different case; the host's CNError.h, which gives CNErrorCodeRecordDoesNotExist as 200; the header of Contacts/CNContactStore.h in the SDK 16.4, which annotates the method NS_AVAILABLE(10_11, NA)
